title: L3 Capstone: Safe Calculator App
story: You can now build programs that handle ANY input without crashing. This is real software engineering. You've mastered Option, Result, match, `?`, guard clauses, pipelines, fallbacks, and error reporting. Now build one program that uses EVERYTHING: a full calculator app that parses expressions, handles errors gracefully, formats results beautifully, and even remembers values — the kind of code you'd be proud to put in a portfolio.
why: This capstone synthesizes every L3 concept into one cohesive application — parsing, validation, error propagation, pattern matching, chaining, and result formatting — proving you can build production-grade, crash-proof programs.
analogy: This calculator is a complete storefront. The evaluate function is the front desk — it takes any request and routes it. The arithmetic handler is the kitchen — it follows recipes (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV) and refuses bad ingredients (non-numbers, zero divisors). The memory system is the back room — you can store and retrieve items by name. Every interaction either succeeds with a receipt (Ok) or gets a polite explanation of the problem (Err). Nothing crashes, nothing is lost, and every case is handled.
try_it: Add memory functions: SAVE stores a value, RECALL retrieves it, CLEAR resets memory. Add a HISTORY command that shows the last 3 results. Add an UNDO command that reverses the last operation. Add a PERCENT command: 'PERCENT 200 15' returns 15% of 200. Add a FACTORIAL command that computes n! using a loop. Can you make the calculator remember up to 5 named variables (SAVE x 10, SAVE y 20, RECALL x)? Add command aliases: '+' works same as ADD, '-' same as SUB.
tips: Build one command at a time — get ADD working perfectly before adding SUB, MUL, DIV
The `split_two` helper is reusable across all arithmetic commands — DRY principle in action
Global `var` declarations work for simple memory — but in production you'd use a struct to encapsulate state
Every command returns Result[Str, Str] so the caller always gets a displayable message or a clear error
common_mistakes: Trying to build all commands at once — start with one, verify it, then copy the pattern
Forgetting the `if sp == 0` check before splitting — a command with no space has no arguments
Using `?` in the main loop's match — you want to collect results, not short-circuit the test suite
